incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor (Nightwing) intentionally disabled GitHub's secret-scanning protections and published a public 'Private-CISA' repository containing plaintext credentials, AWS GovCloud admin keys, RSA private keys, SSH keys and configuration files for dozens of internal CISA systems beginning November 2025.
incidents.impact: One of the most severe U.S. government credential leaks on record; exposed keys granted administrative access to CISA GovCloud, full read/write access to all CISA-IT GitHub repositories, and the ability to hijack CI/CD pipelines. Lawmakers in both chambers of Congress have demanded answers; CISA is still rotating many of the exposed credentials more than a week after notification.

incidents.victim: German university hospitals (Cologne, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Tübingen, Ulm, Mannheim) via Unimed billing provider
incidents.vector: Attackers breached Unimed, a third-party billing service handling invoices for privately insured and self-paying patients at numerous German hospitals, in mid-April 2026.
incidents.impact: Patient data stolen from at least six major university hospitals: ~30,000 patients at Cologne, ~54,000 at Freiburg, ~11,000 at Heidelberg and ~1,600 at Ulm. Stolen data includes names, addresses, treating physicians, treatment-related billing data, and in some cases diagnosis details and bank/payment information. Hospitals have filed criminal complaints and are weighing legal action against Unimed.

incidents.victim: European governmental organizations in Belgium, Italy, Serbia, Spain, Poland (plus entities in South Africa)
incidents.vector: China-aligned APT 'Webworm' shifted focus to Europe, using open-source vulnerability scanners against web servers for initial access and deploying two new backdoors: EchoCreep (which abuses Discord for command-and-control) and GraphWorm (which abuses the Microsoft Graph API and OneDrive).
incidents.impact: Long-running espionage campaign against European government targets between early 2024 and early 2025; threat actor used SOCKS proxies (SoftEther VPN), custom tunneling tools (ChainWorm, SmuxProxy, WormFrp), and staged tooling in GitHub repos and compromised Amazon S3 buckets to remain stealthy and exfiltrate data.

incidents.vector: Phishing emails sent from compromised accounts impersonating Prometheus, Ukraine's largest online learning platform, with PDF attachments linking to a ZIP archive carrying the OysterFresh malware chain (OysterBlues, OysterShuck), with follow-on Cobalt Strike payloads possible.
incidents.impact: Active espionage operation harvesting computer name, OS version, user account and process data from infected Ukrainian government devices; communications hidden behind Cloudflare-fronted infrastructure. Disclosed by Ukraine's CERT-UA alongside a parallel campaign against Ukraine's Delta battlefield management system.

incidents.victim: Technology, aerospace and defense organizations in U.S., Israel, UAE and additional Middle Eastern entities
incidents.vector: Highly tailored spear-phishing using impersonated recruitment lures (e.g., a global air carrier 'Hiring Portal.zip' with fake job-requisition PDFs) and impersonated video-conferencing installers; DLL sideloading and AppDomainManager hijacking disable .NET application security so multi-functional RATs (MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2) can run.
incidents.impact: Six new RAT variants deployed between February and April 2026, with command-and-control traffic routed through three to five Azure-hosted domains per target. The campaign tempo aligned with the regional conflict that began Feb. 28, 2026, indicating coordinated Iranian intelligence collection against high-value technology, defense and telecom targets.

incidents.vector: Kali365, a Telegram-distributed phishing-as-a-service kit, sends branded phishing lures impersonating Adobe, DocuSign or SharePoint directing victims to Microsoft's legitimate device-login flow; when victims enter the supplied code they unknowingly authorize the attacker's device, granting OAuth access and refresh tokens that bypass MFA without ever capturing the password.
incidents.impact: FBI advisory after Proofpoint, IBM, Huntress and Arctic Wolf reported hundreds of attacks throughout April 2026; captured tokens grant immediate, persistent access to Outlook, Teams and OneDrive. In multiple cases attackers also planted malicious inbox rules to suppress alerts and enable business email compromise.

incidents.victim: Unnamed enterprise (Microsoft incident response case study)
incidents.vector: Compromised an end-of-life F5 BIG-IP edge appliance and used trusted SSH access to pivot to an internal Linux host, exploited unpatched Atlassian Confluence for remote code execution, harvested service credentials from Confluence config files, then ran Kerberos relay attacks against Active Directory using CVE-2025-33073.
incidents.impact: Full multi-domain intrusion crossing edge, Linux, SaaS and identity boundaries with sustained hands-on-keyboard access. Microsoft uses the case to underscore that end-of-life perimeter appliances and unpatched internal applications represent a critical attack surface even when not directly internet-exposed.

incidents.vector: Unpatched zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange Server actively exploited in the wild; no vendor patch available at disclosure.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Exchange under 'imminent threat' according to Dark Reading reporting; defenders urged to act now given exposed mail infrastructure and lack of an immediate fix.

incidents.victim: Fuel tank / energy operators (geography per Dark Reading: targets of Iran cyber offensive)
incidents.vector: Cyberattacks expanding Iran's offensive operations against fuel-tank and adjacent energy systems, per Dark Reading reporting tied to the ongoing regional conflict.
incidents.impact: Expansion of Iran's cyber offensive into new energy targets, broadening the scope of disruption operations beyond previously reported sectors.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations across North America, Australia and the UK
incidents.vector: Hired callers conduct sophisticated voice phishing (vishing) against employees' personal cellphones, posing as IT/help desk and directing targets to lookalike subdomains (e.g., enrollms[.]com, passkeyms[.]com); real-time adversary-in-the-middle harvesting captures credentials and MFA codes, then attackers immediately register their own MFA device and use Python/PowerShell scripts (with stolen FedAuth cookies) to bulk-exfiltrate SharePoint, OneDrive, Salesforce and Zendesk data.
incidents.impact: Massive cloud data theft (over a million files in one case), followed by extortion under the 'BlackFile' brand on a dedicated leak site. Pressure tactics include initial multi-million-dollar demands, Gmail-account spam floods, threatening voicemails to C-suite executives, and swatting attacks against company personnel.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack against Taiwan's bullet train operator highlighting gaps in rail-system cybersecurity, per Dark Reading reporting.
incidents.impact: Demonstrated cybersecurity weaknesses in passenger rail; Dark Reading flagged the breach as exposing systemic risk in rail OT/IT environments.

incidents.victim: Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision) — North American factories
incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion against Foxconn's North American factory environments; Nitrogen ransomware group claimed exfiltration prior to encryption (its standard double-extortion pattern targeting Windows and VMware servers).
incidents.impact: Production disrupted at multiple North American Foxconn factories; Nitrogen claims to have stolen 8 TB / 11M+ files including alleged confidential designs from Intel, Apple, Google, Dell and Nvidia, though researchers caution Nitrogen has been inflating claims. Foxconn says affected factories are resuming normal production.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — sophisticated nation-state suspected (UAT-8616) plus multiple criminal clusters
incidents.vector: CVE-2026-20182, a maximum-severity (CVSS 10) authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller/Manager allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to gain administrative access; UAT-8616 also continues to chain CVE-2026-20133, -20128 and -20122 against unpatched SD-WAN Managers, with at least 10 additional clusters deploying webshells (Godzilla, Behinder, XenShell) and tooling (Sliver, AdaptixC2, Cobalt Strike, XMRig).
incidents.impact: Active in-the-wild exploitation; CISA added the bug to the KEV catalog within days. A single compromised SD-WAN controller can reroute traffic, intercept communications, push malicious configs and disrupt entire enterprise overlay networks across on-prem, cloud and FedRAMP deployments.

incidents.vector: Carefully targeted intrusions by APT cluster 'FrostyNeighbor' against government entities in Poland and Ukraine, per Dark Reading reporting.
incidents.impact: Continued Russia-aligned espionage pressure on NATO frontline allies (Poland) and the Ukrainian government during the broader conflict.

incidents.vector: China-aligned FamousSparrow APT established persistence in a South Caucasus energy firm, per Dark Reading reporting.
incidents.impact: Chinese espionage foothold inside an energy operator in a strategically sensitive region; consistent with Beijing's broader interest in regional energy intelligence and pre-positioning.

incidents.victim: Open-source ecosystem (TanStack, Mistral AI, UiPath, and hundreds of npm packages)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — credential theft worm (Mini Shai-Hulud)
incidents.vector: Self-replicating npm supply chain worm ('Mini Shai-Hulud') compromises maintainer accounts and injects payloads into legitimate packages; once executed in a developer environment it harvests developer credentials, API keys, tokens, cloud secrets and cryptocurrency wallets, then uses them to publish further poisoned packages.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of open-source packages compromised in a sprawling supply-chain attack; major projects including TanStack, Mistral AI and UiPath confirmed affected. Source code release of the worm has accelerated copycat clones across the ecosystem.

incidents.vector: A rogue version of Checkmarx's official Jenkins Application Security Testing plugin was published to the Jenkins Marketplace and laced with an infostealer.
incidents.impact: Organizations that installed or updated the trusted Checkmarx Jenkins plugin risk theft of CI/CD secrets, credentials and source code; Checkmarx pulled the rogue release after disclosure.

incidents.victim: Instructure (Canvas LMS) — schools and universities worldwide
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters claimed a second compromise of Instructure following an earlier breach of the Canvas learning-management platform; specific access vector not fully disclosed but extortion-based theft of Canvas-hosted school data.
incidents.impact: Repeat attack against the dominant U.S. K-12/higher-ed LMS vendor; underscores schools' deep vendor dependence and the cascading impact when an education SaaS provider is breached. Instructure later claimed the hackers returned the stolen Canvas data after extortion negotiations.
